d.e: Front, boy. Front, boy. Front, boy. Front, boy. You four boys show Mr. and Mrs. Gilbreth and their seven—-or so—-Irishmen to 503, 504, 505, 506, and 507.

d.t: Containing the maximum possible amount that can fit in the space available.
d.e: The jugs were full to the point of overflowing.

d.t: Complete; with nothing omitted.
d.e: Our book gives full treatment to the subject of angling.

d.t: Total, entire.
d.e: She had tattoos the full length of her arms. He was prosecuted to the full extent of the law.

d.t: Completely empowered, authorized or qualified (in some role); not limited.
d.e: full member

d.t: (informal) Having eaten to satisfaction, having a "full" stomach; replete.
d.e: "I'm full," he said, pushing back from the table.

d.t: (informal, with "of") Replete, abounding with.
d.e: This movie doesn't make sense; it's full of plot holes.

d.t: (informal, of hands, chiefly in the plural) Carrying as much as possible.
d.e: Hang on - my hands are full; just let me put these down.

d.t: (of physical features) Plump, round.
d.e: full lips; a full face; a full figure

d.t: (of the moon) Having its entire face illuminated.
(of clothing) Of a size that is ample, wide, or having ample folds or pleats to be comfortable.
d.e: a full pleated skirt; She needed her full clothing during her pregnancy.

d.t: Having depth and body; rich.
d.e: a full singing voice

d.t: (obsolete) Having the mind filled with ideas; stocked with knowledge; stored with information.
(archaic) Fully; quite; very; thoroughly; completely; exactly; entirely.
Utmost measure or extent; highest state or degree; the state, position, or moment of fullness; fill.
d.e: I was fed to the full.

d.t: (of the moon) The phase of the moon when its entire face is illuminated, full moon.
d.e: It is like, that the brain of man waxeth moister and fuller upon the full of the moon: …

d.t: (gymnastics) A flip involving a complete turn in midair.
(freestyle skiing) An aerialist maneuver consisting of a backflip in conjunction and simultaneous with a complete twist.
(of the moon) To become full or wholly illuminated.
(transitive) To baptise.
To make cloth denser and firmer by soaking, beating and pressing; to waulk or walk.
Involving a full amount of time spent on some activity, especially a job.
d.e: I have a full-time job, working five days a week.

d.t: Spending a full amount of time.
d.e: to work full-time

d.t: Amusement, enjoyment or pleasure.
Playful, often noisy, activity.
Enjoyable or amusing.
d.e: We had a fun time at the party.

d.t: (informal) Whimsical or flamboyant.
d.e: This year's fashion style is much more fun than recent seasons.

d.t: (colloquial) To tease, kid, poke fun at, make fun of.
d.e: Hey, don't get bent out of shape over it; I was just funning you.

d.t: The time ahead; those moments yet to be experienced.
Something that will happen in moments yet to come.
Goodness in what is yet to come. Something to look forward to.
d.e: There is no future in dwelling on the past.

d.t: The likely prospects for or fate of someone or something in time to come.
(grammar) Verb tense used to talk about events that will happen in the future; future tense.
(finance) Alternative form of futures.
(computing, programming) An object that retrieves the value of a promise.
(sports) A minor-league prospect.
Having to do with or occurring in the future.
d.e: Future generations will either laugh or cry at our stupidity.
